findings.title: Any logged-in user can delete arbitrary user accounts via admin.php?action=delete

evidence.why: Only checks that $_SESSION['user_id'] is non-empty; does not check administrator role or account ownership
Target user ID read directly from POST form parameter
Deletes arbitrary user row matching $id with no role check or session ownership constraint

data_flow: mysql_query("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $id") without role or owner check (admin.php:12)
findings.attack_scenario: A normal authenticated user sends POST /admin.php?action=delete with body id=<other_user_id>, deleting another user's account.
findings.impact: Any logged-in user can delete arbitrary user accounts from the users table, causing account loss and denial of service.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the current session belongs to an authorized administrator before allowing user deletion, and use a prepared statement bound to the validated user ID.

checked: inc/auth.php:1-7 (checks $_SESSION['user_id'] login only, no admin role check)
repository root for .htaccess or global access controls (none present)
verification.notes: Verified that admin.php:2 only checks session login via inc/auth.php and performs no role or ownership check before deleting arbitrary user rows in admin.php:11-12.

findings.title: Order shipping address readable by any logged-in user via id parameter

evidence.why: Checks login status only (inc/auth.php:4); does not verify order ownership
Order ID taken from request query string
Queries orders by id alone without constraining user_id to $_SESSION['user_id']
Outputs the fetched order's address without any post-load owner comparison

findings.attack_scenario: Logged-in User A requests GET /order_detail.php?id=<order_id_of_user_B> and reads User B's order address.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can read other customers' order records and personal shipping addresses.
findings.recommendation: Constrain the order lookup by the authenticated user's session ID (AND user_id = ?) using a prepared statement, as done in order_detail_safe.php.
findings.fix_example:
$st = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?');
$st->execute(array($_GET['id'], $_SESSION['user_id']));

checked: order_detail_safe.php:1-9 (confirms orders.user_id is the ownership column)
verification.notes: order_detail.php:6 queries orders by $_GET['id'] alone and outputs $order['address'] at line 8 without scoping to $_SESSION['user_id'].

findings.title: User deletion query interpolates unvalidated POST id into DELETE statement

evidence.why: Source: unvalidated POST parameter id
Sink: unquoted string interpolation into mysql_query with no cast or binding

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user submits a crafted id parameter in the POST body to alter the WHERE clause of the DELETE statement.
findings.impact: Arbitrary deletion of user records or manipulation of database contents accessible to the application database account.
findings.recommendation: Use PDO prepared statements with bound parameters or cast the identifier to an integer before query execution.

verification.notes: Unvalidated $_POST['id'] is directly interpolated into an unquoted numeric context in mysql_query at admin.php:12 with no cast or escaping.

findings.title: MongoDB findOne filter passes raw GET parameters allowing operator injection

evidence.why: Source and sink: $_GET['login'] and $_GET['pass'] passed directly into MongoCollection::findOne filter without scalar type enforcement

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user supplies array query parameters for login or pass so PHP constructs nested associative arrays interpreted as MongoDB query operators.
findings.impact: Unauthorized query filter manipulation and credential check bypass on the shop.members collection.
findings.recommendation: Validate that login and pass are scalar strings or explicitly cast them to string before passing to findOne.

verification.notes: $_GET['login'] and $_GET['pass'] are passed directly into MongoCollection::findOne at mongo_find.php:5 without scalar string validation or casting, allowing array operator injection.

findings.title: MongoDB $where query concatenates unvalidated GET parameter into JavaScript expression

evidence.why: Source and sink: $_GET['n'] concatenated directly into MongoDB $where JavaScript string

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user provides a crafted n query parameter that breaks out of the string literal inside the $where JavaScript predicate.
findings.impact: Arbitrary JavaScript predicate evaluation inside the MongoDB query context and unauthorized disclosure of shop.members documents.
findings.recommendation: Replace the $where JavaScript evaluation with a standard field equality filter using scalar string values.

verification.notes: $_GET['n'] is concatenated directly into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression at mongo_find.php:6 with no sanitization.

findings.title: Order detail query concatenates unvalidated GET id into SELECT statement

evidence.why: Source: unvalidated GET parameter id
Sink: unquoted concatenation of $id into mysql_query

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user supplies a crafted id query parameter to modify the SQL query structure and retrieve arbitrary rows.
findings.impact: Unauthorized disclosure of order records and other tables accessible to the database user.
findings.recommendation: Use a PDO prepared statement with bound parameters and scope the query to the authenticated user.
findings.fix_example:
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?');
$stmt->execute(array($_GET['id'], $_SESSION['user_id']));

verification.notes: $_GET['id'] is concatenated unquoted into mysql_query at order_detail.php:6 with no integer cast or parameter binding.

findings.title: Product search query concatenates GET keyword sanitized only with addslashes

evidence.why: Source and weak sanitizer: $_GET['q'] passed only through addslashes()
Concatenated into SQL LIKE clause
Sink: executed via mysql_query without parameter binding

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user supplies a crafted search term where addslashes fails to prevent quote breakout (such as under multibyte connection encodings) to alter the SQL query.
findings.impact: Unauthorized reading of database tables accessible to the application database account.
findings.recommendation: Use PDO prepared statements with bound parameters instead of addslashes and string concatenation.
findings.fix_example:
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE ?');
$stmt->execute(array('%' . $_GET['q'] . '%'));

verification.notes: $_GET['q'] is only passed through addslashes() at search.php:5 before concatenation into LIKE at line 8 and execution via mysql_query at line 11; addslashes is not an adequate SQLi defense per injection-patterns.md §3.

findings.title: Product search query concatenates unvalidated GET sort parameter into ORDER BY clause

evidence.why: Source: unvalidated GET parameter sort
Concatenated directly into ORDER BY clause without allow-list validation
Sink: executed via mysql_query

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user passes arbitrary SQL expressions in the sort query parameter to inject into the ORDER BY clause.
findings.impact: Unauthorized data extraction via boolean/time-based inference or error-based SQL injection across database tables.
findings.recommendation: Validate the sort parameter against a strict exact-match allow-list of permitted column names and directions.

verification.notes: Unvalidated $_GET['sort'] is concatenated directly into the ORDER BY clause at search.php:9 and executed via mysql_query at line 11 without allow-list validation.

findings.title: Product category query interpolates unvalidated GET cat parameter in heredoc SQL

evidence.why: Source and interpolation: $_GET['cat'] interpolated directly into heredoc SQL string $q
Sink: heredoc query executed via mysql_query without binding

findings.attack_scenario: An authenticated user provides a crafted cat query parameter to break out of the single-quoted string in the WHERE clause.
findings.impact: Unauthorized disclosure of data from any table accessible to the application database account.
findings.recommendation: Use a PDO prepared statement with a bound parameter for the category filter.

verification.notes: $_GET['cat'] is interpolated directly into the heredoc SQL string at search.php:14 and executed via mysql_query at line 16 without escaping or parameter binding.

findings.title: Admin user lookup accessible to any logged-in user without role or ownership check

evidence.why: Enforces session login only (!empty($_SESSION['user_id'])); no administrator role or ownership check
Target user ID taken directly from query parameter uid
Queries users table by arbitrary uid without binding to $_SESSION['user_id'] or verifying admin role (note: $r is not rendered in this file)

data_flow: mysql_query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " . $uid) without role or owner filter (admin.php:8)
findings.attack_scenario: A regular logged-in user sends GET /admin.php?action=view&uid=<other_user_id> and triggers a database lookup on another user's record without administrator privilege or ownership verification.
findings.impact: Unauthorized query execution against arbitrary rows in the users table by any authenticated user; however, the result resource $r is not fetched or output in admin.php, so data is not directly exposed in the HTTP response (rated low per bola-patterns.md section 6).
findings.recommendation: Enforce an administrator role check from the server-side session before dispatching admin actions, or restrict the query to $_SESSION['user_id'] if intended for self-service profile lookup.

checked: post-query usage of $r in admin.php:8-9 (never fetched or output)
verification.notes: No admin role or ownership check exists before querying users by $_GET['uid'] at admin.php:8; severity remains low because $r is not rendered.
